messages:
jason-oncall: Heads up — several customers started hitting elevated p95/p99 latency after the runtime rollout started this morning (v5.3.1 ramp). Putting triage here.
deploy-bot: rollout v5.3.1 -> 30% traffic (staged) started at 2026-03-17T08:12:34Z :rocket:
jen-support: ACME reported timeouts and 2-3s extra tail on /v1/embeddings. They pasted request_id=rcq-9f2a-33 and example timestamp 2026-03-17T08:25:01Z. Customer says impact is user-facing (search latency). Can we get quick repro guidance?
maria-runtime: Thanks. Canary didn't show obvious spike but canary size small. Preliminary hypothesis: scheduler change + kernel selector fallback path is triggering more slow-paths for short sequences. Also verify KV cache hit-rate — rollout may have invalidated some caches.
ryan-sre: Can we grab a flame/tail sample from the runtime for those request_ids? Use trace id from the request if available. If not, sample full request logs for tenant=acme-org between 08:22-08:30. Example query:
```
logs.query("tenant=acme-org AND request_id=rcq-9f2a-33", start=08:22, end=08:30) | json | select(duration_ms, kernel, scheduler)
```
maria-runtime: Good. Also run quick comparison of kernel selection distribution between v5.3.0 and v5.3.1 for the embeddings route:
```
infra/metrics diff --from v5.3.0 --to v5.3.1 --metric kernel.selector.percent --route embeddings --window 1h
```
eli-ml: Note that model seq lengths for ACME are short (~16 tokens). A scheduler tweak that favors batching could increase p99 if it delays short requests waiting for batch fill.
jen-support: ACME provided two more request_ids: rcq-1b4c-77, rcq-4d2e-11. I uploaded them to the shared drive: https://redwood.internal/triage/acme/2234567890
ryan-sre: I pulled logs. Sample tail snippet:
```
[08:25:01.123] request_id=rcq-9f2a-33 duration_ms=1412 kernel=fallback_x scheduler=latebind kv_cache_hit=false
[08:25:01.126] request_id=rcq-1b4c-77 duration_ms=1589 kernel=fallback_x scheduler=latebind kv_cache_hit=false
```
maria-runtime: Those lines are informative — kernel=fallback_x looks like the quantized path fallback. We should check kernel selector thresholds; maybe a conservative threshold changed in v5.3.1 causing more fallbacks.
tonys-ops: (cc @maria-runtime) Can we mitigate without full rollback? If it's kernel selector hysteresis, we can temporarily route ACME (and other affected tenants) to the previous runtime variant.
maria-runtime: Yes — two immediate mitigations:
1) Pause ramp of v5.3.1 (stop incrementing traffic).
2) Add a route override for affected tenants to v5.3.0.
ryan-sre: To pause ramp:
```
deploy-control pause-rollout --version v5.3.1 --reason "p99 spike investigation"
```
maria-runtime: To route a tenant back to v5.3.0 (example):
```
curl -X POST https://control.redwood/api/v1/routing/override \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -d '{"tenant":"acme-org","route":"embeddings","target_version":"v5.3.0","ttl":"2h"}'
```
jen-support: I can apply the override for ACME and one other impacted tenant. Will confirm once done.
sam-exec: Customer impact looks medium->high for search UX. Recommend we open a customer incident (notify ACME) and offer a temporary workaround (route override). If rollback is needed we'll do a full roll-back of v5.3.1.
eli-ml: While mitigations are in flight, collect perf diffs for short-seq cohort. Use replay tool to simulate 1k ACME-like requests against v5.3.0 and v5.3.1 locally to reproduce the p95/p99 gap.
maria-runtime: Repro steps for the replay (put in triage doc):
1) run `replay/simulate --tenant acme-org --route embeddings --count 1000 --seq-len 12`
2) compare p50/p95/p99 in the `results.json`
3) if reproduced, run `bisection` toggling these flags: kernel-selector, scheduler-latebind, quant-compat
```
replay/compare --v1 v5.3.0 --v2 v5.3.1 --metrics p95,p99 --cohort short-seq
```
ryan-sre: If replay reproduces, plan a binary bisect: rollback kernel-selector commit range first (fast), then scheduler commit range, then quant changes. Keep canary frozen.
jen-support: I applied route override to ACME and TestCorp. Confirmed lower latency within 10 minutes. ACME accepted temporary workaround and wants ETA for root cause.
maria-runtime: Great — action plan summary:
- pause ramp (done?)
- route overrides for impacted tenants (jen applied to two)
- run replay + bisect to identify changeset
- if bisect points to single commit, hotfix + small rollback OR patch
- communicate to customer with ETA
jason-oncall: Thanks team. Assign owners: @maria-runtime lead bisect, @ryan-sre collect traces/flamegraphs, @eli-ml run replay, @jen-support customer comms. Keep updates here. If bisect shows kernel-selector as root cause we can ship a hotfix with a config flag to revert threshold.
ryan-sre: I'll attach trace snapshots and a short flame snippet in 30m. Also enabling higher sampling for embeddings route for next 1h.
maria-runtime: If anyone finds strong evidence of KV-cache coldstart being the real cause (low hit rate in logs), call that out — caching fixes are trickier but we can add warmup or routing to warmed hosts.
sam-exec: I'll prepare a customer-facing summary once we confirm root cause. Keep me posted.
jen-support: Noted. I'll update the ACME incident channel and push current mitigation details.
maria-runtime: Update 08:51: replay reproduced 1.6x p99 increase locally when kernel-selector falls back to fallback_x. Next step: isolate commit that changed selector thresholds.
jason-oncall: Good progress. If we see clear repro and patch ETA <2h, call it a hotfix; otherwise plan rollback. Closing loop in ~1h or when root cause confirmed. :white_check_mark:
